subject: Materials Science
title: Thermal Shock Resistance
description: A micro-lesson that makes Thermal Shock Resistance usable.

hook.text: Pour boiling water into a cold glass and it shatters. Pour it into a Pyrex beaker and nothing happens.

buildup.text: Thermal shock occurs when rapid temperature change creates internal stress that exceeds the material's strength.

discovery.text: Low expansion, high conductivity, and high strength together make a material thermal-shock resistant.

twist.text: Ceramics have high strength but high expansion and low conductivity — a deadly thermal shock combination.

climax.text: Space shuttle tiles survived re-entry heat by being porous silica — incredibly low expansion and conductivity.

punchline.text: Thermal shock kills from within — the surface cools but the core can't keep up.

quiz.question: What property combination resists thermal shock?
options: Low expansion, high conductivity, and high strength
High density and high melting point
